transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Zoe Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Singh (Head of ML, AtlasNova), David Morales (SRE), Aisha Khan (VP Product), Ben Ko (Security), Evan Park (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Check-in on production usage and cost trends; discuss recent latency spikes and fallback behavior.
- Pilot readiness: pilot SOW, dev VPC access, bench to validate 99th percentile latency and token cost.
- Security questions around KMS integration, SSO, audit logs; Redwood to send SOC2 docs and keynotes.
- Next steps: share pricing + SOW, schedule benchmark, setup temporary VPC access.

Topics noted:
- Usage & cost variance (May spike + token mix)
- Reliability incidents and mitigation (failover, routing)
- Dedicated vs Hosted for pilot vs GA
- Security controls (KMS, SSO, audit logs, retention)
- Roadmap items: autoscaling tweaks, KV cache tuning, trace visibility

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we wanted to run through a short health and pilot readiness huddle for AtlasNova, um I see most folks on the call, nice to meet new faces.
[00:16] Priya Singh: hey Maya thanks, quick heads up we have a 45 minute block, we wanna focus on three things — usage/cost, reliability, and the pilot ramp scope.
[00:31] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. I'll jump into some telemetry after Maya gives the bigger-picture notes.
[00:39] Aisha Khan: hi, hi — we're mostly product here to confirm timelines and acceptance criteria for pilot.
[00:45] David Morales: SRE chiming in for the latency + incident review.
[00:49] Ben Ko: security — I'll surface the compliance checklist and KMS questions.
[00:55] Maya Chen: great. Quick context: May had a usage bump around the new release (text-summarization for support tickets), we've been seeing token mix shift toward long-form generation which changed cost profile; Redwood is flagging both cost and a couple 99th percentile latency blips on May 22 and May 29. We'll propose pilot SOW that covers dedicated capacity for the test window to stabilize p99 while we tune batching and the KV cache.
[01:24] Priya Singh: the cost hit was bigger than we expected — can you run through the token cost breakdown?
[01:31] Liam O'Connor: sure, so from our ingestion telemetry — short summary: 60% of tokens were from long-form responses (avg 1.3k tokens per request for the new summarizer), that drove both GPU contention and higher per-token compute, also some tail requests kept sessions open which prevented KV eviction. So net — higher GPU-hours and slight p99 increases.
[01:58] Evan Park: when you say KV eviction, are you referring to the K-V cash, the cache in the runtime?
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: yeah sorry, K-V cache, kp, the KV cache for attention keys — sometimes transcription picks it up funny — but yes we saw increased KV working set.
[02:14] Priya Singh: okay that explains the memory pressure. Can you quantify what enabling dedicated pool for the pilot would cost vs hosted burst?
[02:25] Maya Chen: initial estimate: for a 4-week pilot with a small dedicated pool (2 x A6000-equivalent nodes), rough ballpark is $XXk — we'll send exact pricing; the benefit is consistent p99 and isolation, plus we can pin quantized model artifacts. Hosted burst would be cheaper short-term but less predictable at p99 under long tails.
[02:46] Aisha Khan: we're sensitive to run rate, will the pilot give us a deterministic unit cost we can model?
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: yes, dedicated gives deterministic throughput pricing — you'll be able to model per-hour capacity and map to token throughput; we can also provide a mid-pilot usage report.
[03:05] David Morales: about those p99 blips — do you have traces? any correlation to region or to particular model versions?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: good question: two main correlates: one, bursty long generations from the summarizer causing batch-formation delays; two, an intermittent network jitter in the eu-west region around May 29 (we routed through fallback region and that created extra hop). We have traces for both — I'll share the trace IDs after the call.
[03:38] Ben Ko: on the security side we have a few must-haves: KMS integration for keys, SSO/SAML, per-request audit logs, and data residency notes. Does Redwood offer HSM-backed KMS?
[03:53] Zoe Patel: yes, we support customer-managed keys and integrations with AWS KMS and some HSM providers, there's a configuration path for private deployments. We'll share the integration guide.
[04:10] Ben Ko: also need retention/TTL control on logs and redact PII in traces, is that configurable?
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: we have log retention policies and you can configure redaction rules in the console; RBAC controls exist for access to audit logs. We'll point to the docs — link will be in the follow-up.
[04:29] Priya Singh: can Redwood do a small performance benchmark with our test corpus — we'd like to validate p50/p95/p99 on our real workload.
[04:37] Maya Chen: absolutely, that's part of the next steps. Liam will set up a benchmark run — we typically run with a dev VPC or a sample dataset in s3 and measure token cost and p99 under a 1k qps spike pattern.
[04:51] Evan Park: regarding dev VPC — we need to understand what access to provide, and any egress requirements.
[04:57] Liam O'Connor: we'll request a temporary IAM role and a peered VPC endpoint for the test nodes; no permanent inbound required. We'll document the minimal IAM policy.
[05:08] Aisha Khan: timeline — we want pilot running by mid-June if possible, what's realistic?
[05:14] Maya Chen: if VPC access and SOW are signed this week we can start provisioning the dedicated pool and schedule the benchmark the week of Jun 15. So mid-June is feasible but tight.
[05:25] Priya Singh: ok we'll try to get Ben and Evan the compliance list by Monday.
[05:29] Ben Ko: yes I'll compile it.
[05:31] David Morales: another ops question — you mentioned autoscaling policies earlier, can we set stricter burst limits to keep costs down?
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: yes, autoscale has configurable policies — target latency, target utilization, and we can set hard caps on burst nodes; for cost control we recommend a mix of prefix caching and conservative batch windows to avoid runaway GPU-hours.
[05:55] Priya Singh: prefix caching — is that the same as the KV cache you mentioned?
[06:00] Liam O'Connor: related but different — prefix caching stores frequent prompt prefixes at route-level so they bypass full decode on repeated queries, KV cache refers to internal attention key/values per session. Both help cost but at different layers.
[06:13] Aisha Khan: on the roadmap items — are any of the improvements (KV tuning, improved batching heuristics) going to land before our pilot?
[06:21] Liam O'Connor: we're shipping a few runtime improvements in late June — better batch formation heuristics and an update to the cache eviction policy. We can enable experimental flags for your pilot to test those sooner.
[06:34] Priya Singh: experimental flags — does that affect SLA?
[06:36] Zoe Patel: experimental flags are opt-in for pilots; we recommend running them in parallel to the stable path and we won't change production routing without explicit sign-off.
[06:45] Evan Park: are there any benchmarks comparing quantized variants? we might accept slightly lower quality for big cost wins.
[06:52] Liam O'Connor: we have comparative perf profiles in the model catalog, including 4-bit quantized variants — typical token-cost reductions are 30-60% depending on sequence length, with small quality delta; we'll attach the catalog link in follow-up.
[07:06] Priya Singh: quality delta is a concern — we need to validate with our evaluation set.
[07:10] Maya Chen: agreed — part of the benchmark is a quality pass against your eval set. We'll run A/B on quantized + full precision and report rouge/accuracy metrics.
[07:19] David Morales: earlier you said occasional region fallbacks caused extra hops — can we prioritize the eu-west deployment?
[07:26] Liam O'Connor: yes, routing policies can pin region or prefer local capacity; for pilot we can route solely through eu-west nodes to avoid cross-region hops.
[07:35] Ben Ko: about audit logs, who on the Redwood side has access? we need least-privilege assurances.
[07:41] Zoe Patel: access is limited to customer-scoped roles and the ops on-call; we can provide a list of Redwood roles and provide an RSA for audit if needed.
[07:50] Priya Singh: ok let's talk acceptance criteria — for us pilot success = p99 under 2s for the short-form flows and under 6s for long-form summarization at target qps, token cost within projected budget, and no data exfil issues.
[08:06] Maya Chen: noted — we'll bake those into the SOW (p99 SLA targets, cost targets, and security checklist).
[08:12] Aisha Khan: any blockers from Redwood for starting?
[08:15] Maya Chen: main blocker is signing SOW + granting the dev access. Also Ben's security questions need to be answered. We'll aim to get all artifacts over by Tue/Wed.
[08:25] Priya Singh: great. Can we get a mid-pilot checkpoint weekly sync?
[08:29] Zoe Patel: yes weekly check-ins are standard — we'll put that on the SOW cadence.
[08:33] David Morales: hypothetical: if the dedicated pool still has p99 noise, what's the fallback?
[08:38] Liam O'Connor: fallback options: scale up the pool temporarily, enable a model variant with lower latency (pruned/quantized), or route heavy tails to a secondary lower-cost batch path with slightly higher latency but bounded cost. We'll discuss tradeoffs during benchmark tuning.
[08:57] Priya Singh: question — do you have a reference for similar customers with long-form summarization workloads?
[09:02] Maya Chen: yes we have a retail customer (anonymized) who ran a similar pilot; I can share a redacted case study and numbers.
[09:09] Aisha Khan: ok please share.
[09:11] Ben Ko: also please include the SOC2 and ISO attachments in the follow-up.
[09:15] Zoe Patel: will do.
[09:17] Maya Chen: quick recap of action items — I'll share SOW and pricing; Liam will schedule the benchmark and supply traces; Ben/Evan to provide security and VPC access; we'll have weekly syncs once pilot starts.
[09:34] Priya Singh: sounds good, thanks all.
[09:36] Matthew (off): speaker mislabeled as Matthew but that's actually Evan — little audio hiccup.
[09:40] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links: pricing SOW (drive link), security pack (secure link), and benchmark kickoff calendar.
[09:50] END
